external_entities.name: colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague who signs in through the identity broker and uses applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
external_entities.notes: The text also says colleagues may use their own devices at home; it does not place the colleague in a specific zone.

external_entities.name: franchise colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague from a franchise store who is vouched for by the franchise identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The text does not state where franchise colleagues run or connect from.

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The system that supplies colleague group membership changes overnight.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.
external_entities.notes: The text does not state the HR system's location or control boundary.

external_entities.name: franchise identity provider
external_entities.description: An identity provider operated for franchise colleagues that vouches for their sign-in.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The text does not identify which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, signs tokens, supplies public keys, imports group membership, and writes sign-ins to an audit log.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The broker runs on the corporate network. Tokens are valid for twelve hours and cannot be pulled back before expiry.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that uses token groups to authorize price changes and transaction voids for every store.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications.
processes.notes: The console runs on the corporate network and does not check which store the colleague belongs to.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: A store holding the signing key used by the identity broker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.
data_stores.notes: The text does not state where the key store runs or whether it is encrypted at rest.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory containing colleagues and their groups.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: The text does not state whether the directory is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: A log to which the broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route. The text does not state whether the log is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A colleague signs in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token to a signed-in colleague.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: The token carries the colleague's staff id and group list.
data_flows.data_description: A token carrying the colleague's staff id and groups

data_flows.name: present token
data_flows.description: A colleague presents a token to the store admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing staff id and group membership

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the public signing key from the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: Public half of the token-signing key

data_flows.name: update membership
data_flows.description: The HR system supplies group membership changes to the identity broker overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night
data_flows.notes: The text says the broker pulls the changes, but the flow is represented as the broker initiating the pull from the HR system.

data_flows.name: franchise sign-in
data_flows.description: A franchise colleague signs in through the identity broker using the franchise identity provider's vouching.
data_flows.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.
data_flows.notes: The text does not specify the protocol or authentication mechanism beyond the separate identity provider vouching.

data_flows.name: vouch sign-in
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in
data_flows.notes: The text does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

data_flows.name: use signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker uses the signing key kept in the key store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state the storage access protocol.

data_flows.name: keep directory records
data_flows.description: The identity broker keeps colleague and group records in its directory.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: write audit log
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: It is unknown whether franchise-route sign-ins are included.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: own devices at home
trust_boundaries.description: Colleagues' own devices at home from which they may sign in.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

trust_boundaries.name: franchise identity provider
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them

assumptions.assumption: The directory is confidential because it holds colleague identities and group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source says the directory contains colleagues and the groups they are in.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log is confidential because it holds sign-in records associated with colleagues.
assumptions.basis: The source says the broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.

assumptions.assumption: The key store is confidential because it holds the token-signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source says the key store holds a signing key.
